summaries.summary: An anonymous quote distrusts a MS minion over Windows ME, Vista and 8 producing self-guiding AI.
An anonymous quote suggests an AI would help Patients confide information because a robot cannot judge them.
Dogmatism is defined, examples are contrasted, and psychology suggests computationally modelable aspects like over-confidence and strong emotions.
A statistical model of dogmatism validates psychological theories through feature sets and applies the model to four questions.
R1 asks what kinds of topics, such as guns and LGBT, attract the highest levels of dogmatism.
R2 asks how dogmatic beliefs cluster.
R3 asks how dogmatism influences social media conversation, and R4 asks how user behaviors relate to dogmatism.
A predictive model classifies dogmatic Reddit posts using a released corpus of 5,000 annotated Reddit posts.
Domain-independent psychological features support theory, with less confident language and absent cognition terms linked to dogmatism.
The 5,000-post-trained model analyzes millions of Reddit posts, finding diverse dogmatic topics, trait evidence, and conversational vicious cycles.
Reddit posts are a natural starting point for untangling domain-independent linguistic features of dogmatism.
The training dataset contains 5000 posts sampled from politics, business, science, AskReddit, and the Reddit frontpage.
Amazon Mechanical Turk crowdworkers labeled the Reddit dataset on a 5-point Likert scale for dogmatism.
Crowdworkers imagined holding a different opinion and rated constructive conversation likelihood with the commenter.
Option (5) describes unlikely substantive conversation and likely insults or lowered discourse after respectful disagreement.
Option (4) describes deeply rooted opinions but view exchange without much degeneration.
Option (3) describes unlikely mind-changing but easy conversation and mutual understanding.
Option (2) describes a clear opinion with likely openness to alternative viewpoints.
Option (1) describes unset opinions, possible mind-changing, and comments conveying no opinion.
Quality control restricted the task to Masters workers and provided examples for each scale point.
A highly dogmatic (5) comment example mentions BofA, Wells, executives, squad cars, and established facts.
The text introduces a minimally dogmatic (1) comment example.
A minimally dogmatic comment agrees and asks about compiling a trance yogi playlist and platform preference.
Each comment received three independent AMT annotations, summed into an aggregate dogmatism measure shown in Figure 1.
Krippendorff's α is 0.44 overall, 0.69 for top and bottom quartiles, motivating training on those quartiles.
The study examines dogmatism using LIWC and 17 of LIWC's categories.
LIWC category counts are normalized, odds ratios compare top and bottom quartiles, and Mann-Whitney U with Holmes correction tests significance.
Certainty is associated with dogmatic comments at 1.52 odds, while tentativeness is associated with absence of dogmatism at 0.88 odds.
LIWC insight terms verbalize cognition and are associated with non-dogmatic comments at 0.83 odds.
LIWC perception captures sensory language and is associated with non-dogmatic comments at 0.77 odds.
Relativity is associated with non-dogmatic comments at 0.80 odds, but comparison does not reach significance.
First person singular pronouns show 0.46 odds, while second person singular and third person plural show 2.18 and 1.63 odds.
Present tense is a positive dogmatism signal at 1.11 odds, while past tense is negative at 0.69 odds.
Negative emotion at 2.09 odds and swearing at 3.80 odds signal dogmatism, while positive emotion is not significant.
Interrogative language at 1.12 odds and negation at 1.35 odds are additional positive dogmatism signals.
Correlated linguistic signals cumulatively affect dogmatism, illustrated by progressively removing hedges and adding certainty.
Linguistic feature sets build a classifier predicting dogmatism and enabling scalable analysis of millions of Reddit comments.
The prediction task tests cross-validation within Reddit and domain independence on held out New York Times comments.
Balanced dogmatic and non-dogmatic classes use 2,500 Reddit training comments and 500 New York Times testing comments.
Logistic regression compares BOW, SENT, LING, and combinations, with BOW using TF-IDF and L2 penalties of 1.5.
BOW reaches AUC 0.853 within Reddit and 0.776 on New York Times, while linguistic features boost results to 0.881 and 0.791.
Results suggest psychology-inspired linguistic features predict dogmatism and generalize across new domains.
The BOW+LING model labels millions of new Reddit posts with dogmatism probabilities from 0 to 1 for four research questions.
The analysis begins by examining dogmatism across Reddit sub-communities, expecting abortion or climate change higher and cooking lower.
The study samples 1.6 million posts from 2007 to 2015 and computes average dogmatism for subreddits with at least 100 posts.
Politics and religion subreddits rank high, hobbies rank low, and cringepics has the highest average dogmatism level.
SubredditDrama discusses internet fights and provides a sanity check that the model captures robust dogmatism.
The study examines whether dogmatism is domain-specific or a deeper personality trait through subreddit relationships among users.
The study samples 1000 Reddit users and 10 million posts, computing mutual information between dogmatic subreddit links.
Table 4 shows dogmatism clusters linking Libertarianism and business to political and topical subreddits, unlike user-post links.
Politics dogmatism disproportionately links to science, technology, IAmA, and AskReddit with reported binomial-test p-values.
The authors ask whether high-level user behaviors beyond linguistic features are similarly predictive of dogmatism.
Using 1000 users and 10 million posts, activity, breadth, focus, and engagement significantly predict average dogmatism in a linear regression model ($R^2=0.1$, $p<0.001$).
The authors ask how interacting with a dogmatic comment affects a conversation and whether otherwise non-dogmatic users become more dogmatic.
They sample 600,000 conversations triples from Reddit with structure A1 $\rightarrow$ B $\rightarrow$ A2 and use linear regression to model B's dogmatism impact on A2.
The B feature coefficient is positively associated with dogmatism ($p<0.001$), and the effect holds across dogmatic and non-dogmatic subsets and after removing B's words.
Unlike the presented computational models, psychology usually measures dogmatism through survey scales that have been updated and improved for psychometric validity.

Surveys relate dogmatism to confrontation, moral conviction, religiosity, cognitive flexibility, and problem solving, while this work examines Reddit user behaviors using a language model of dogmatism.
Ertel captured dogmatism linguistically with a small lexicon, McKenny related it to student essay argument quality, and this work applies supervised models with broader linguistic categories.
Related work studies cognitive style, trolls, impartial language on twitter, politeness, deception, and authority, inspiring the feature sets used here.
Other work examines argument justifications and what makes an argument likely to win, while this model may enable deeper probing of such questions.
The authors constructed the first corpus of social media posts annotated with dogmatism scores, explored linguistic features, built a predictive model, and applied it to Reddit.
The authors ask whether the computational model could help users shed dogmatic beliefs and suggest new avenues for encouraging pro-social behavior in online communities.
